1.pericope_label: Therefore, thou son of man, prophesy against Gog, and say, Thus saith the Lord God; Behold, I am against thee, O Gog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal: And I will turn thee back, and leave but the sixth part of thee, and will cause thee to come up from the north parts, and will bring thee upon the mountains of Israel: And I will smite thy bow out of thy left hand, and will cause thine arrows to fall out of thy right hand. Thou shalt fall upon the mountains of Israel, thou, and all thy bands, and the people that is with thee: I will give thee unto the ravenous birds of every sort, and to the beasts of the field to be devoured. Thou shalt fall upon the open field: for I have spoken it, saith the Lord God. And I will send a fire on Magog, and among them that dwell carelessly in the isles: and they shall know that I am the Lord. So will I make my holy name known in the midst of my people Israel; and I will not let them pollute my holy name any more: and the heathen shall know that I am the Lord, the Holy One in Israel. Behold, it is come, and it is done, saith the Lord God; this is the day whereof I have spoken.

schools.summary: Head the passage as the general announcement of the destruction, question the received rendering of a word occurring nowhere else, and read the judgment as universal and apocalyptic.
Deny that the turning back means turning from Israel, and identify the country to be burnt with a still-future empire.
Read every element of the chapter historically of the Seleucid campaign, and take the bow as standing for all other weapons.
Accounts for the repetition as line upon line, and reads the mountains first as a place of temptation and then as one of execution.

positions.position: Antiochus and his campaign: the Persian archers, the Syrian troops, the auxiliaries from the Euxine, and the rout in Israel itself.
A still-future destruction, the country to be burnt being the Ottoman empire and the slaughter wrought by Christian princes or by judgments from heaven.
A universal judgment: it falls on the distant country as well as the invading army, and the isles are named to show its reach.
The notable day of recompences against the last great enemies of the church.

outliers.claim: Challenges the rendering that leaves a sixth part of the invader, since the word occurs nowhere else and the assumed derivation from the numeral is probably wrong, all the ancient versions giving a sense of leading and turning instead.

Notes that the enemy comes from the north as the Chaldeans did, quotes the proverb that every evil comes from the north, and observes that the Roman empire was long afterwards overrun from that quarter.

9.pericope_label: And they that dwell in the cities of Israel shall go forth, and shall set on fire and burn the weapons, both the shields and the bucklers, the bows and the arrows, and the handstaves, and the spears, and they shall burn them with fire seven years: So that they shall take no wood out of the field, neither cut down any out of the forests; for they shall burn the weapons with fire: and they shall spoil those that spoiled them, and rob those that robbed them, saith the Lord God. And it shall come to pass in that day, that I will give unto Gog a place there of graves in Israel, the valley of the passengers on the east of the sea: and it shall stop the noses of the passengers: and there shall they bury Gog and all his multitude: and they shall call it The valley of Hamon–gog. And seven months shall the house of Israel be burying of them, that they may cleanse the land. Yea, all the people of the land shall bury them; and it shall be to them a renown the day that I shall be glorified, saith the Lord God. And they shall sever out men of continual employment, passing through the land to bury with the passengers those that remain upon the face of the earth, to cleanse it: after the end of seven months shall they search. And the passengers that pass through the land, when any seeth a man’s bone, then shall he set up a sign by it, till the buriers have buried it in the valley of Hamon–gog. And also the name of the city shall be Hamonah. Thus shall they cleanse the land.

schools.summary: Denies the seven years can be literal and supports it with an arithmetic reductio, and rejects both derivations offered for the valley's name.
Take the burning and the burying plainly, and read the naming of the city as a memorial of the multitude buried there.
Allow a good deal of literal meaning within a figurative frame, and explain why weapons that might have served for defence were destroyed.
Turns the labour of cleansing into a lesson, that times of great deliverance should be times of reformation.

debates.question: Can the seven years and seven months be taken literally?

positions.position: No: one army's weapons cannot fuel a nation for seven years, and the figure was inserted to send us beyond the letter; a million burying two corpses daily would mean three hundred and sixty million bodies.
Figurative, but admitting a good deal of literal meaning, since many of the defeated died hidden and were not all found at once.
Credible as it stands, the need of fire in that country being much less than in ours.
Plainly, so that they would have no need to fetch wood, having a sufficiency of armour.

debates.question: What is the valley of the passengers?

positions.position: A real trade road east of the lake, by which merchants went down from Syria into Egypt.
Probably an imaginary thoroughfare, since the same word recurs in a plainly different sense and cannot be derived from the passing of the invaders.

outliers.claim: Raises the difficulty that arms which might have served for their own defence are destroyed, and answers that it was done in testimony that God was their defence and that on him only they relied.
Explains why the cleansing mattered so much, since under the law the extremest defilement of all was caused by a dead body or human bones, from which the land could be purified only by burial.

17.pericope_label: And, thou son of man, thus saith the Lord God; Speak unto every feathered fowl, and to every beast of the field, Assemble yourselves, and come; gather yourselves on every side to my sacrifice that I do sacrifice for you, even a great sacrifice upon the mountains of Israel, that ye may eat flesh, and drink blood. Ye shall eat the flesh of the mighty, and drink the blood of the princes of the earth, of rams, of lambs, and of goats, of bullocks, all of them fatlings of Bashan. And ye shall eat fat till ye be full, and drink blood till ye be drunken, of my sacrifice which I have sacrificed for you. Thus ye shall be filled at my table with horses and chariots, with mighty men, and with all men of war, saith the Lord God. And I will set my glory among the heathen, and all the heathen shall see my judgment that I have executed, and my hand that I have laid upon them. So the house of Israel shall know that I am the Lord their God from that day and forward. And the heathen shall know that the house of Israel went into captivity for their iniquity: because they trespassed against me, therefore hid I my face from them, and gave them into the hand of their enemies: so fell they all by the sword. According to their uncleanness and according to their transgressions have I done unto them, and hid my face from them.

schools.summary: Notes a curious mingling of the figurative and the literal, warns that the sacrifice figure must not be pressed, and holds the promised knowledge realised only in germ.
Answers the oddity of addressing creatures not yet in being, and makes the display of glory the ultimate end of the whole event.
Explain the summons from the custom of feasting on a sacrifice, and rebut a slander that the invitation was addressed to the Jews.

debates.question: How far may the sacrifice figure be pressed?

positions.position: Not far: the figure occurs in other prophets and is not to be pushed beyond its purpose.
As far as it will go: a sacrifice offered to God's own justice, and so great that none ever was or will be like it.
By way of custom: the friends and neighbours of a sacrificer are invited to feast upon the offering.

outliers.claim: Rebuts Voltaire by name for saying the Jews ate human flesh and were here invited to eat their enemies, calling it a most unprincipled falsehood since it is the fowls and beasts that God invites.

Raises the oddity that the address is made to creatures not then in being which could not have understood it, and answers that they will be gathered partly by instinct and partly by a direction of providence.

25.pericope_label: Therefore thus saith the Lord God; Now will I bring again the captivity of Jacob, and have mercy upon the whole house of Israel, and will be jealous for my holy name; After that they have borne their shame, and all their trespasses whereby they have trespassed against me, when they dwelt safely in their land, and none made them afraid. When I have brought them again from the people, and gathered them out of their enemies’ lands, and am sanctified in them in the sight of many nations; Then shall they know that I am the Lord their God, which caused them to be led into captivity among the heathen: but I have gathered them unto their own land, and have left none of them any more there. Neither will I hide my face any more from them: for I have poured out my spirit upon the house of Israel, saith the Lord God.

schools.summary: Explains why the promise of return stands at the close, as the first step of a long course of events and the one of especial comfort to exiles.
Sets the promise in a latter-day scheme, the people brought at last to repentance and faith, with the divine presence never again removed.
Argue from the incompleteness of the historical return to a greater one, and read the past tense of the outpouring as a promise.

debates.question: How far does the promise of restoration reach?

positions.position: Beyond the historical return, since all who chose had liberty to go back but many stayed, so that none being left points to a larger restoration in the gospel dispensation.
To a latter-day conversion, after which the worship and presence of God will never be removed from them again.
Only the first step is in view here, whose full effect the exiles could not have measured.

outliers.claim: Corrects the tense of the outpouring, taking the past form as a promise of what God will do, and describes the Spirit's work as enlightening, quickening and cleansing until they become a praise in the earth.
Reports an alternative rendering by which the clause about shame becomes a statement that they shall bear it, rather than a note of time after which the promise takes effect.
